name: BACH_0006_FSIM_stain3
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Normal (84%)** · Confident · Read in turn

Single-class conformal set, second-model agreement and 5/5 Normal neighbors all support it [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Normal 84%, InSitu 15%, Invasive <1% | Clear lead over InSitu |
| Conformal set | {Normal} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.997 / 78th percentile | Input looks typical |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes | Independent model concurs |
| Similar cases | 5 of 5 Normal | Neighbors match |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules, two-layered epithelium** (regions 2, 4, 11) · ↓ invasive · Strongest concept term (−1.8); its spot check failed · Unreliable
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 4, 8, 11) · ↑ invasive · Concept model links it to invasive; above typical [F3] · Validated
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 6, 7, 9) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; spot check 20/20 [F4] · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect the classifier. This case leans on normal lobules, which is Unreliable (0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Stain degradation (severity 3) distorts appearance; InSitu still holds 15%.
- Stroma in regions 4, 8, 11 is truly tumor-infiltrated, despite P(invasive) under 1%.

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 1**: highest per-region invasive probe risk (46%); look for invasion or in situ change.
2. **Regions 4, 8, 11**: decide whether the stroma is tumor-infiltrated or benign fibrous.
3. **Regions 2, 4, 11**: confirm two-layered lobular epithelium; its AI spot check was 0/20.
